articles.title: Draft NUREG: Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities
articles.summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing for public comment a draft report entitled, NUREG-1307, Revision 21, "Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities." This report, which is revised periodically, explains the formula acceptable to the NRC for determining the minimum decommissioning fund requirements for nuclear power reactor licensees, as required by NRC regulations. Specifically, this report provides the adjustment factor and updates the values for the labor, energy, and waste burial escalation factors of the minimum formula.

articles.title: Notice of Availability of a Pest Risk Analysis for the Importation of Fresh Passion Fruit From Viet Nam Into the United States
articles.summary: We are advising the public that we have prepared a pest risk analysis that evaluates the risks associated with the importation of fresh passion fruit (Passiflora edulis) for consumption from Viet Nam into the United States. Based on the analysis, we have determined that the application of one or more designated phytosanitary measures will be sufficient to mitigate the risks of introducing or disseminating plant pests or noxious weeds via the importation of fresh passion fruit from Viet Nam into the United States. articles.content: Iraqi Line returns to Gulf container trade after 50 years - Splash247 ICTSI Iraq’s national shipping line is returning to scheduled container services in the Gulf after more than half a century, as the country seeks to rebuild maritime connections disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz crisis. According to Alphaliner, Iraqi Maritime Line is deploying the 902 teu Basrah on an eight-day shuttle linking Jebel Ali in Dubai with Umm Qasr, Iraq’s principal container gateway. The first sailing was scheduled to depart Jebel Ali yesterday, arriving in Umm Qasr two days later. Iraq’s transport ministry has described the initiative as the national carrier’s first regular Gulf operation since the mid-1960s. The relaunch comes as Iraqi container supply chains have been radically reshaped since the Hormuz shipping crisis erupted at the end of February. Growing volumes have been diverted to Jordan’s Red Sea port of Aqaba before travelling overland into Iraq through the Trebil border crossing. According to the Jordan Shipping Association, Aqaba handled 37,182 Iraq-bound transit containers during the first seven months of 2026, compared with just 3,599 during the corresponding period last year, a 933% increase. Maersk has introduced landbridge services connecting Aqaba with Iraq, while CMA CGM has offered alternative routings through Aqaba for southern Iraq and Turkey’s Mersin for northern destinations. articles.content: Gestion Maritime makes ultramax debut with China order - Splash247 Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering Monaco-based shipowner Gestion Maritime is moving into the ultramax segment with an order for three 64,000 dwt bulk carriers at China’s Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering. The Danilo Fumarola-led company has booked the trio for delivery between late 2028 and early 2029, expanding beyond its traditional panamax and kamsarmax fleet. The vessels are costing in the low $30m range apiece, putting the overall investment at more than $90m. Gestion Maritime currently operates six panamax and kamsarmax bulkers and has recently trimmed its fleet through asset sales. The latest investment will bring smaller and more modern tonnage into a portfolio built largely around Japanese- and South Korean-built ships. The company, whose roots date back to 1908 and the Corrado shipping family, has traditionally pursued an asset trading strategy, buying ships when values ease and disposing of tonnage during stronger markets. In 2019, it exited the product tanker sector by selling two 2015-built MR tankers to Hafnia interests for $31m each, returning its focus to dry bulk. The newbuilding deal adds another international owner to Nantong Xiangyu’s growing customer base. The Chinese shipbuilder marked the delivery of its 100th ultramax bulker in July and has continued to attract orders for the 63,500 to 64,000 dwt segment. articles.content: Aker BP and Höegh Evi secure EU funding for North Sea CO2 storage project - Splash247 Aker BP Norwegian offshore producer Aker BP and maritime infrastructure specialist Höegh Evi have secured €223m ($260m) from the European Union Innovation Fund for their Atlas carbon transport and storage project in the North Sea. The project aims to establish a large-scale carbon capture and storage (CCS) network that links industrial emitters across Europe to permanent storage facilities on the Norwegian continental shelf through a combination of collection hubs, specialised CO2 carriers, and subsea injection infrastructure. Atlas has an initial design capacity of 6m tonnes of CO2 annually, with potential to expand beyond 10m tonnes as the European carbon storage market develops. Under the proposed system, the project would aggregate captured CO2 at regional export hubs near industrial clusters before transporting it aboard dedicated low-pressure carriers to the offshore storage site. CO2 would be injected directly through subsea infrastructure into a saline aquifer more than 2,000 m below the seabed, removing the need for extensive onshore pipeline networks. The project was recognised as an EU Project of Mutual Interest in April 2026, acknowledging its potential to provide cross-border carbon transport and storage infrastructure. articles.content: Trump’s Plan to Revive Sanctioned Tankers Faces Tough Sell Russia's shadow fleet vessels wait in the unofficial anchorage area in the Gulf of Finland near Vaindloo, Estonia April 10, 2026. REUTERS/Ints Kalnins Trump’s Plan to Revive Sanctioned Tankers Faces Tough Sell Bloomberg Total Views: 271 October 20, 2026 (Bloomberg) — A US plan to rehabilitate sanctioned tankers to boost oil supply may attract only a sliver of the dark fleet, as existing contracts, complex compliance checks and sky-high freight rates reduce incentives for would-be sellers. The measure — detailed on Monday, just weeks ahead of the US midterm elections — is the latest in a string of efforts by the Trump administration to cool crude and fuel prices driven higher by months of war in the Persian Gulf and the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Soaring gasoline and diesel costs in particular have fueled affordability concerns among US voters. articles.content: MSC tipped for another 20 megamaxes in China - Splash247 Yangzijiang Shipbuilding Mediterranean Shipping Co (MSC) has reportedly added another 20 megamax containerships at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries, further expanding its already massive orderbook as global newbuilding commitments climb to their highest level in more than a decade. According to liner consultancy Linerlytica, Gianluigi Aponte’s carrier has booked 20 additional 24,000 teu vessels at the Dalian-based shipbuilder, representing another 480,000 teu of future capacity. The latest deal takes MSC’s programme of vessels exceeding 20,000 teu at Hengli to 62 ships, Linerlytica said in its latest weekly market report. No contract value, delivery dates or propulsion specifications have been disclosed for the new batch. MSC has built up a substantial pipeline at Hengli since the two companies signed a strategic cooperation agreement in 2024. The liner giant initially contracted ten 21,000 teu and ten 24,000 teu LNG dual-fuel newbuildings, before returning for six 22,000 teu ships last year. The latest reported order adds another sizeable block of capacity to an expansion programme that already dwarfs those of rival carriers. At the end of September, Alphaliner data cited by Splash put MSC’s operated fleet at around 7.4m teu, representing 21.5% of global liner capacity, with another 2.94m teu on order. articles.content: Spodumene shipments triple as battery boom creates new dry bulk trades - Splash247 Tata Motors The seaborne trade in spodumene, a lithium-bearing mineral essential for battery production, is emerging as one of dry bulk shipping’s fastest-growing niche cargoes, with volumes more than tripling over the past five years. New research from Greek shipbroker Ursa Shipbrokers shows global shipments reached 4.04m tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, up 11.9% year-on-year and a record for the period. Annual shipments have climbed from just 1.58m tonnes in 2020 to 5.08m tonnes last year, reflecting the rapid expansion of lithium mining and growing demand from electric vehicle manufacturers and battery storage projects. Australia dominates the trade, accounting for 81% of shipments during the first nine months of this year, equivalent to 3.26m tonnes. Brazil ranked second with 570,000 tonnes, while smaller quantities originated in Canada, Mozambique and Vietnam. China remains overwhelmingly the principal destination, receiving 88% of global seaborne spodumene cargoes, equivalent to 3.56m tonnes, reflecting its dominant position in lithium refining and battery manufacturing. The trade is providing growing employment opportunities for smaller bulk carriers. Ultramaxes accounted for 39.6% of vessel deadweight employed in spodumene shipments this year, with handysizes representing a further 46%. articles.content: Apache braces for offshore strike across seven platforms - Splash247 Apache More than 160 offshore workers, employed by US oil and gas producer Apache, are set to stage a 24-hour strike across seven North Sea installations on Wednesday, with union Unite warning the industrial action could disrupt the strategically important Forties Pipeline System. The walkout will begin at 6 am on October 21 and end the following morning. A second 24-hour stoppage is scheduled for November 4. The affected installations are Forties Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta, and Echo, alongside Beryl Alpha and Beryl Bravo. Unite said shutting down the Forties Charlie platform could drop pipeline pressure, potentially forcing the entire Ineos-operated Forties Pipeline System (FPS) offline and disrupting production from other North Sea operators. The FPS handles oil and gas liquids from more than 80 offshore fields and the St Fergus gas terminal, with a nominal capacity exceeding 600,000 barrels per day. Apache, however, has rejected suggestions that the strike could shut down the wider network. The company said contingency plans included retaining experienced personnel on Forties Charlie to support third-party production, even if output from all five Apache-operated Forties platforms was suspended. Apache maintained that any resulting pressure reduction would be comparable to a routine maintenance shutdown. The dispute centres on a pay offer that Unite claims amounts to a real-terms pay cut for many workers

articles.summary: The Greek finance ministry said on Thursday it was implementing sanctions in place linked to Iran and that it backed efforts to effectively combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism.
articles.content: Greece Says It is Implementing Sanctions Linked to Iran Russia's shadow fleet vessels wait in the unofficial anchorage area in the Gulf of Finland near Vaindloo, Estonia April 10, 2026. REUTERS/Ints Kalnins Greece Says It is Implementing Sanctions Linked to Iran Reuters Total Views: 61 October 22, 2026 ATHENS, Oct 22 (Reuters) – The Greek finance ministry said on Thursday it was implementing sanctions in place linked to Iran and that it backed efforts to effectively combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism. The statement comes after the US Treasury Department said on Wednesday it imposed sanctions on Karnakis & Karnakis, a law firm based in Greece and Panama, saying it had for years provided legal assistance to Iranian shipping networks. The Treasury also said that the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued an administrative subpoena to advance an investigation into a Greek bank, which it did not name. The Greek finance ministry said it had taken note of the US Treasury statement, adding that “all available information is being evaluated, and appropriate measures are being taken in accordance with established procedures and applicable national, EU, and international law.” (Reporting by Angeliki Koutantou; Editing by Aidan Lewis) (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026. articles.content: China's green corridor push hits commercial reality check - Splash247 CMB.TECH China has emerged as a major player in the global green shipping corridor movement, with at least 21 initiatives linked to the country, although most remain in their early stages and only one has progressed towards commercial operation, according to a new report from the Global Maritime Forum. The study, released during the organisation’s annual summit in Shanghai, shows that China accounts for nearly a fifth of the world’s green shipping corridor initiatives, having added ten new projects in 2025 alone. However, of the 21 initiatives identified by the end of June this year, 12 were still at the initiation stage, five were exploring feasibility, three had reached preparation and just one had entered the realisation phase. The most advanced is the Australia-East Asia Iron Ore corridor, involving the deployment of ammonia-powered bulk carriers between Australia’s Pilbara region and China. The report also highlights how much of the sector’s future fuel supply is increasingly concentrated in China. The country accounts for around 80% of global green methanol production capacity that has passed final investment decision and more than 40% of comparable green ammonia capacity. Kevin Bangston, president and CEO of Daimler Truck Financial Services USA LLC, handled the view from the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Goetz Johanning, head of strategy and realization for the North American financial services arm, moderated. The session was set up as a conversation rather than a presentation, and the candor showed. OK By Chang Dong-woo WASHINGTON, Oct. 16 (Yonhap) -- South Korea has condemned recent deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels targeting civilian infrastructure and threatening commercial shipping in the Red Sea, calling on the U.N. Security Council to strengthen sanctions to cut off weapons supplies to the group. South Korean Ambassador to the United Nations Cha Ji-hoon made the remarks during a Security Council debate on the Middle East held Thursday, warning that the attacks pose serious threats to global peace, maritime security and energy supplies. "We condemn such attacks and urge an immediate halt to all attacks against civilians," Cha said during the debate. "We call on this council to strengthen sanctions, to effectively cut off the supply of weapons to the Houthis." Cha said the Houthis' recent attacks targeting civilian infrastructure and threats to commercial navigation in the Red Sea were posing "severe risks to global peace as well as maritime and energy security." articles.content: Ceva Logistics puts Paack in charge of last-mile parcel delivery - FreightWaves LAST CHANCE F3 is Oct 27-28 - use promo code: LUCKYLAST50 for $1,295 tickets Register → × Industry giant Ceva Logistics on Friday announced that it has merged France-focused last-mile delivery subsidiary Colis Privé into newly acquired Paack, which operates a dense delivery network in Spain and Portugal, presenting a single brand identity to the market. Ceva Logistics, a top-five global logistics company by gross revenue and part of Marseilles, France-based CMA CGM Group, acquired Paack in early August to expand its last-mile delivery business in Europe. It acquired Colis Privé, which also operates in Belgium and Luxembourg, in 2022. The unified Paack brand will be rolled out progressively to customers and partners beginning in January, Ceva said in a news release. When the tentative deal was first announced last summer, the expectation was that Colis Privé would absorb Paack. The combined business delivers 150 million parcels annually through a network of 17,000 out-of-home delivery points — 8,000 each in France and Spain, and 1,500 in Belgium. Paack has about 490 employees. It also operates six urban delivery stations in France. The couriers also deliver to individual residences. articles.content: European shipowners demand bigger share of EU carbon revenues - Splash247 ECSA European shipowners are calling for a threefold increase in the carbon allowances earmarked to support shipping’s energy transition, arguing that the sector contributes almost twice its share of emissions to the EU Emissions Trading System’s auction revenues. A study published by European Community Shipowners’ Associations (ECSA) estimates that the proposed Sustainable Maritime Alternative Propulsion (SMAP) mechanism needs at least 330m allowances, compared with the 110m currently envisaged by the European Commission. The association puts the required support at around €30bn ($33.6bn), aimed at narrowing the cost gap between conventional marine fuels and cleaner alternatives. The proposal forms part of the ongoing revision of the EU ETS and remains subject to approval by the European Parliament and Council. According to ECSA, maritime transport accounts for approximately 10% of emissions covered by the trading system but purchases almost 20% of the allowances auctioned.Unlike several industrial sectors, shipping has not received free allowances since joining the system in 2024. With the phase-in period completed, shipping companies must surrender allowances covering 100% of their emissions falling within the ETS framework from the 2026 emissions year. articles.content: China Merchants and COSCO move to exit Qingdao ore terminal - Splash247 China Communications Construction Company China Merchants Port and COSCO Shipping Ports are joining forces with IMC to sell a controlling stake in an iron ore terminal at China’s Qingdao port, setting a minimum price of CNY1.92bn ($287m). The three shareholders have launched a public tender for their combined 70% holding in Qingdao Port Dongjiakou Ore Terminal, according to Hong Kong stock exchange disclosures. China Merchants Port and COSCO Shipping Ports each hold 25% of the terminal company, while Singapore-based IMC owns another 20%. Qingdao Port International retains the remaining 30%. The stakes are being offered as a single package through the China Beijing Equity Exchange, with bidding open until November 11. The minimum consideration has been set at $287m, including $102m apiece for the holdings of China Merchants and COSCO. The terminal company is responsible for the construction, operation and management of iron ore handling facilities at Dongjiakou, one of Qingdao’s main bulk cargo areas. Dongjiakou has been developed to accommodate some of the world’s largest ore carriers. Its 400,000 dwt iron ore terminal entered service in 2013, giving the port the ability to receive very large ore carriers employed in trades between Brazil and China. The post Evos raises $9M to build AI operators for industrial businesses appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Evos raises $9M to build AI operators for industrial businesses - FreightWaves AI startup Evos raised $9 million in pre-seed funding to develop autonomous software operators for small and midsized industrial businesses, including freight brokerages, the company announced Wednesday. This comes as the company looks to automate routine work without requiring businesses to replace their existing software. The round was co-led by Uncork Capital and Field Ventures, with participation from Crosslink Capital, Utopia Capital Management, Sandwith Ventures and angel investors. Evos said it surpassed $1 million in annual recurring revenue four weeks after launching. The company did not disclose its valuation or the number of customers using its platform. How it works Evos is developing AI operators that learn how employees make decisions and carry out specific business functions within a company’s existing systems. Rather than requiring employees to prompt an AI tool for every task, the operators are designed to manage an assigned function independently once their decisions consistently match those of experienced workers. The approach targets smaller industrial businesses where operational knowledge often rests with experienced employees rather than documented procedures. articles.title: Tesla staffs up Nevada Semi plant as fleet orders stack up
articles.summary:

The post Tesla staffs up Nevada Semi plant as fleet orders stack up appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Tesla staffs up Nevada Semi plant as fleet orders stack up - FreightWaves Tesla had 103 job openings with Semi in the title posted at its Sparks, Nevada, truck plant as of Oct. 16, according to Tesla’s careers site. The listings come three weeks after the plant started high-volume Semi production on Sept. 24. The hiring is for a 1.7-million-square-foot factory designed to build 50,000 trucks a year, as fleets line up orders for a truck Tesla first showed in 2017. Tesla has not said how many Semis the plant is building now. Before the dedicated line opened, the Semi fleet numbered just under 200 pilot trucks, delivered to customers including DHL, PepsiCo and US Foods. Drayage carrier IMC Logistics ordered 50 Semis this month, following WattEV’s 370-truck order in May. Tesla was also named lead manufacturer on a 2,500-truck order through the ZET SCALE alliance in September, though the alliance did not say how many of those trucks will be Semis. Tesla CEO Elon Musk told analysts in July, “We have started production with the Tesla semi-truck.” The company’s second-quarter shareholder update said production was expected to begin later in the year. Semi openings span assembly to dispatch The Semi listings include quality technicians for stamping, body-in-white and powertrain; equipment maintenance technicians for general assembly and the drivetrain; and a CDL driver, a dispatcher and an endurance fleet driver. Several are night-shift roles, including a battery production supervisor

articles.summary:

The post Larger UPS air hub in Philippines boosts Asia service levels appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Larger UPS air hub in Philippines boosts Asia service levels - FreightWaves United Parcel Service’s new air hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines is 15 times larger than its predecessor, enabling the express carrier to provide up to two days faster delivery for customers within Asia and improve connectivity across its global network. UPS (NYSE: UPS) spent $80 million on the expansion project, which includes specialized handling areas for healthcare, high-tech and manufacturing customers with time-sensitive and temperature-sensitive shipments. Parcel handling capacity increased to an average daily volume of 46,000, with maximum processing capacity of 15,000 pieces per hour, according to a news release on Thursday. The announcement marks the first time UPS has disclosed the size of the capital expenditure to expand its Clark hub, which now covers 323,000 square feet. UPS now operates 170 flight segments into and out of Clark every week, connecting businesses across Asia Pacific, India, Europe and the United States in as little as one business day. The new hub has also created nearly 600 jobs, the company said. In August, the U.S. Department of Transportation approved the transfer of six UPS flying rights between Hong Kong and Warsaw, Poland, and Hanoi, Vietnam, to Clark Airport to support growing trade flows between the Philippines and Hong Kong. articles.content: West Africa's ore boom meets China's growing VLOC armada - Splash247 Winning West Africa is fast becoming dry bulk shipping’s biggest growth engine, with its mineral export boom poised to absorb the equivalent of another 120 capesizes by 2030. UK consultancy Tradeviews forecasts in a new report that shipments from the region will surge 50% from 2025 levels to 303m tonnes by the end of the decade, with Guinea’s giant Simandou iron ore project leading the charge. Crucially for shipowners, the long voyages to China will magnify the impact on vessel demand. “West Africa looks set to remain the fastest growing long-haul source of dry bulk cargo,” Tradeviews stated. The growth is already evident. The five West African exporters covered by the consultancy shipped 160.1m tonnes in their principal trades during the first eight months of this year, up 25% year on year. Liberian iron ore exports nearly doubled to 10.1m tonnes. Tradeviews expects regional exports to reach 267m tonnes next year, with Guinean iron ore shipments climbing to 45m tonnes in 2027 and approximately 112m tonnes by 2030. Bauxite exports, meanwhile, are forecast to retreat from a peak of nearly 194m tonnes this year to 153m tonnes by 2030 as Guinea pushes ahead with domestic alumina processing. A capesize round voyage between Guinea and China takes approximately 78 days, compared with just 29 days on the Australia-China route.
